headline: Denmark Exposes 8.8 Million Residents
lede: Unauthorized access to Denmark’s central person register exposed names, addresses, CPR numbers, and other personal data at national scale. Authorities have revoked the offending company’s access and opened an investigation into how legitimate credentials became an extraction channel.

headline: Huawei and Qualcomm Reset Patent Lines
lede: Huawei and Qualcomm announce a multi-year cross-license spanning 5G, computing, AI, and networking. Qualcomm will also acquire selected Huawei patents, pending regulatory approval, turning years of intellectual-property tension into a cleaner commercial arrangement.

headline: A Mac Intrusion Tests the Agent Future
lede: An unpatched Screen Sharing service opened a path to root access and a Monero miner; a persistent Claude agent helped detect and remediate the intrusion. The episode exposes a quieter conflict between macOS permission boundaries and machines expected to act autonomously on their owners’ behalf.

headline: A 125B Model Runs on Gaming Hardware
lede: Strata spreads a large mixture-of-experts model across VRAM, system memory, CPU resources, and SSD storage. The result is private local inference on consumer machines, with speed, quality, startup time, and hardware capacity traded explicitly in the design.

headline: Tippett’s Lost Workshop Finds a Home
lede: After Tippett Studios closed, an anonymous buyer rescued 90 archival discs from an auction and placed their contents in the Internet Archive. Production photographs, tests, interviews, and visual-effects records now remain available beyond the studio’s shuttered walls.

headline: Doom’s Game Loop Moves Into SQL
lede: A CedarDB experiment stores Doom’s world, entities, and rendering logic in relational tables, then queries complete frames at the original 35 Hz. It is an impractical engine and an excellent demonstration of how far set-based operations can be pushed.

headline: VB6 Reappears Inside the Browser
lede: A browser-native recreation brings Visual Basic 6’s forms, controls, modules, and event-driven workflow back to life. The Northwind-style demo is part preservation project, part programming toy, and a reminder of how approachable visual tools once felt.

headline: Backup Is a Habit, Not a Destination
lede: The Tao of Backup returns to the unglamorous discipline of preserving what matters and proving that it can be restored. Configuration files, storage choices, secrets, retention, and recovery tests each carry a different part of the burden.

headline: Infidel’s Desert Corrupts the Machine
lede: A 1984 Infocom routine mistakes a global index for a memory address, eventually overwriting the Z-machine’s abbreviation table. The rare failure is a compact lesson in latent corruption, compiler behavior, and the state that tests never inspect.

headline: How Babylon Taught the Gods
lede: A study of first-millennium BCE Babylonia finds religious knowledge embedded within scribal education, professional preparation, and everyday social life. Divine names, myths, rituals, and local traditions formed part of a curriculum transmitted through both written exercises and oral instruction.
